findings.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.java canManage() uses hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), granting manage-all-groups rights to callers with only view scope; should check MANAGE alone like canManage(GroupModel), otherwise view-only admins can create/update/delete groups

GroupPermissionsV2.java throws UnsupportedOperationException from isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource(group), etc., breaking existing callers like AdminPermissions.registerListener and admin REST endpoints, causing 500s or event-listener failures

GroupPermissionsV2.java getGroupIdsWithViewPermission adds the authorization resource UUID instead of the group ID (resource name), so IDs placed into UserModel.GROUPS never match actual group IDs in user search; should use groupResource.getName()

UsersResource.searchForUser and BruteForceUsersResource removed the per-user usersEvaluator::canView filter, relying solely on the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute; unsafe if any user storage provider ignores that attribute in searchForUserStream, and the GROUPS set is built from different scopes (VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS) without double-checking

Scope mismatch in GroupPermissionsV2: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects groups granted VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS while canView(GroupModel) accepts VIEW/MANAGE, causing groups visible in group endpoints to be missing from the ID set and user searches returning no users from them

GroupPermissions.java getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (V1) early-return now only checks root.users().canView() where it previously also checked canManage(), a behavior regression restricting GROUPS sets for admins with fine-grained manage-only permission on all users

GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest lacks tests covering the V2 UnsupportedOperationException paths and the negative test that VIEW-only on all-groups cannot manage groups (would have caught the canManage bug); also contains a stray double semicolon in a field declaration

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.java throws UnsupportedOperationException from isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource(group), etc., breaking existing callers like AdminPermissions.registerListener and admin REST endpoints, causing 500s or event-listener failures

adjudication.rationale: In `MgmtPermissionsV2`, `groups()` is overridden to return `new GroupPermissionsV2(...)`. `GroupPermissionsV2` overrides management-style methods like `setPermissionsEnabled(GroupModel, boolean)`, `isPermissionsEnabled(GroupModel)`, `resource(GroupModel)`, and `getPermissions(GroupModel)` to throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (“Not supported in V2”). The diff shows an existing caller in `AdminPermissions.registerListener`: on group/role removal it executes `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getGroup(), false);`. If `management(...)` resolves to `MgmtPermissionsV2` (as implied by the introduction of V2 implementations), this will throw at runtime, breaking the listener (and likely yielding 500s where similar methods are invoked).

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsersResource.searchForUser and BruteForceUsersResource removed the per-user usersEvaluator::canView filter, relying solely on the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute; unsafe if any user storage provider ignores that attribute in searchForUserStream, and the GROUPS set is built from different scopes (VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS) without double-checking

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser`, the diff removes the explicit `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` from the `searchForUserStream(...)` result and now passes the raw stream into `toRepresentation(...)`, relying on the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute (`session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)`) to constrain results. The diff does not show any replacement filter at this call site, so permission enforcement now depends on lower layers honoring that session attribute. However, the finding overstates that `BruteForceUsersResource` removed such a filter—there wasn’t a `usersEvaluator::canView` filter there in the shown code, only a refactor to inline the stream.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Scope mismatch in GroupPermissionsV2: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects groups granted VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS while canView(GroupModel) accepts VIEW/MANAGE, causing groups visible in group endpoints to be missing from the ID set and user searches returning no users from them

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, user search filtering via `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is intentionally tied to *member visibility* (`VIEW_MEMBERS`/`MANAGE_MEMBERS`), not general group visibility (`VIEW`/`MANAGE`). `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` collects group IDs where the caller can view/manage members, and `UserPermissions.canViewByGroup()` was updated to use `root.groups()::canViewMembers`, which in V2 checks `VIEW_MEMBERS`/`MANAGE_MEMBERS`. Meanwhile group endpoints (`GroupsResource`, `GroupResource`) filter with `groupsEvaluator::canView`, which correctly uses `VIEW`/`MANAGE` for group visibility. So the claimed “scope mismatch causing missing users” is not a verifiable defect from the diff; it reflects a misunderstanding that group VIEW/MANAGE should imply viewing members/users, which the new scopes explicitly separate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissions.java getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (V1) early-return now only checks root.users().canView() where it previously also checked canManage(), a behavior regression restricting GROUPS sets for admins with fine-grained manage-only permission on all users

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() from `if (root.users().canView() || root.users().canManage())` to only `if (root.users().canView())`, but in this codebase `root.users().canView()` already returns true when the caller has MANAGE authority as well (UserPermissions.canView() checks admin roles MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS and also allows either VIEW or MANAGE scopes). Therefore an admin with “manage-only” permission on all users would still satisfy canView() and get the same early-return behavior, so the claimed regression is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest lacks tests covering the V2 UnsupportedOperationException paths and the negative test that VIEW-only on all-groups cannot manage groups (would have caught the canManage bug); also contains a stray double semicolon in a field declaration

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added test `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest`, there is a stray double semicolon in the field declaration: `private final GroupRepresentation topGroup = new GroupRepresentation();;` (harmless but real). Also, the test class does not include a negative case asserting that an “all-groups” permission with only `VIEW` does *not* allow managing groups (it only tests `MANAGE` in `testManageAllGroups` and `VIEW` in `testViewGroups`), and it does not exercise any of the V2 methods in `GroupPermissionsV2` that explicitly `throw new UnsupportedOperationException(...)` (e.g., `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `viewMembersPermission`, etc.). These are specific, diff-grounded test coverage gaps rather than a direct functional defect in the test itself.
